results.title: Mixed-effects models with nested data
results.content: # Mixed-effects models with nested data. *Mixed Effects Models and Extensions in Ecology with R.* Springer. * Mixed-effects models maximize use of info in the data, compared to 2-stage analysis. #### Linear mixed-effects models. * Step 2: fit model with gls (so linear regression model can be compared with mixed-effects models). * Step 4: fit the model. Side note: instead of using the `lm()` function for my linear model, I use the `gls()` function in case I need to add a variance later on, this way I can compare the model with no variance structure to the model with the variance structure. The AIC is lower for the random-intercept model and the L.Ratio is quite high, so the p-value is low (p<0.0001) which is good evidence that the random-effects model is a better fit for the data, and that each species does in fact have its own specialization relationship with forest cover.
